public_rationale: In ITPro's October 19, 2026 report, Microsoft described its Loughton withdrawal as a decision about a single site [e1]. On October 16, 2026, NiSource announced a long-term energy agreement for Microsoft's northwest Indiana campus [e2]. These records do not establish a company-wide expansion halt by a named company or a collective halt by all four [e1, e2]. They therefore cannot settle the predicted effect of such a halt on debt issuance [e1, e2]. Neither source supplies comparable spending figures to settle the tens-of-billions cost clause [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence concerns Microsoft and does not comprehensively establish expansion decisions across all four companies.
No debt-issuance response is matched to a verified qualifying expansion halt.
The forecast leaves unclear whether one company or all four must halt, and supplies no deadline or numerical response thresholds.
The spending clause lacks a defined period, accounting basis and allocation among companies.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Building more capacity will cost Microsoft, Google, Meta and Amazon tens of billions of dollars, but if they stop building capacity it will be an immediate signal that they've overbuilt, sending shockwaves through the industry and killing data center debt issuance.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Meta and Amazon are stuck in a terrible situation where building more capacity will cost them tens of billions of dollars, but stopping building capacity will be an immediate signal that they’ve overbuilt capacity, sending anxiety-strewn shockwaves through the industry and killing data center debt issuance.

from_speaker: building more capacity will cost them tens of billions of dollars
an immediate signal that they’ve overbuilt capacity
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading requires a material halt to capacity expansion by a named hyperscaler, rather than cancellation or delay of one project.
It is unclear whether one company's halt or a collective halt is required; both readings must be checked before scoring.
Killing issuance means a shutdown or near-shutdown of new data-center borrowing, not merely wider spreads.
Immediate requires a prompt, identifiable market response; no numerical time window is supplied.
The spending clause gives no accounting basis, period or allocation among the four companies. Dollars are read as US dollars from context.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying halt occurs, investors promptly interpret it as evidence of overbuilding, and data-center debt issuance stops or nearly stops because of that signal. The spending clause requires separate comparable financial evidence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying halt occurs, yet substantial new data-center debt issuance continues through the ensuing market response without the predicted shutdown.

evidence.locator: Microsoft spokesperson response following Latest Videos
evidence.explanation: Microsoft explicitly limits the withdrawal to one site. This rejects that event as proof of the required expansion halt, rather than contradicting the forecast's market consequence.
The agreement indicates continued Microsoft campus development close to the reported cancellation. It does not establish the expansion status of every named company or measure construction spending.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verify a qualifying expansion halt, checking both the individual-company and collective readings. Obtain prompt investor reactions and completed issuance records showing whether the halt signaled overbuilding and caused borrowing to stop or nearly stop, or substantial issuance continued. Separately obtain comparable financial evidence for the capacity-spending clause.
